title: Los Retros Frontman Mauri Tapia Charged With Felony Counts in California; Label Cuts Ties
excerpt: Mauricio 'Mauri' Tapia, 26, frontman of indie band Los Retros, has been charged in California with four felony counts. He has not entered a plea.
content:
Mauricio "Mauri" Tapia, the 26-year-old frontman of the California indie band Los Retros, has been charged in Ventura County with four felony counts of unlawful acts with a child under the age of 10, according to court records reported by USA TODAY and the Ventura County Star. The charges are allegations, not a conviction. Tapia has not entered a plea, and he is presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.

The Charges

Prosecutors filed the four felony counts in Ventura County Superior Court on October 12. The filing also carries special allegations: that the alleged victim was vulnerable, and that Tapia allegedly took advantage of a position of trust. Special allegations are claims prosecutors must prove in court; if proven, they can increase a sentence following a conviction.

The Ventura County Sheriff's Office is investigating the case. Authorities have released no further details publicly.

Timeline

  • October 8, 2026: Tapia is arrested.
  • October 9, 2026: He is booked into Ventura County jail, with bail set at $3 million.
  • October 12, 2026: He is charged in Ventura County Superior Court with four felony counts, along with the special allegations. His arraignment is continued, and he does not enter a plea.
  • October 15, 2026: His label, Stones Throw Records, publicly responds to the allegations.
  • October 22, 2026: His next scheduled court date.

Who Is Los Retros?

Tapia, of Moorpark and Oxnard, California, founded Los Retros in 2016. The band built a large international following, drawing about 2.8 million monthly listeners on Spotify, and its best-known song, "Someone To Spend Time With," has passed 200 million streams. Los Retros performed at the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival in April 2026, and the album "Odisea" was released on April 3, 2026.

The Label Responds

On October 15, Stones Throw Records said it had learned of the allegations on October 14 and takes them extremely seriously. The label said it is "taking steps to disassociate ourselves from Tapia and his work." Tapia's scheduled performance at the label's Stones Throw 30 festival had been cancelled before the label learned of the allegations. As of October 18, his releases still appeared on the label's digital platforms.

Tapia's next court appearance is scheduled for Thursday, October 22, 2026. Webb Watch 956 will follow the court record as the case proceeds.
